newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Blue chip firms pull Morocco's weekly exchange dow.
newsitem.headline: Blue chip firms pull Morocco's weekly exchange dow.

text.p: The market blue chip stocks brought the Casablanca bourse lower during the week ending Friday compared with the previous week, stockbrokers said.
The all-share index closed at 435.19 points from 437.99 points last Friday.

"The bourse index was marked by a slight fluctuation and decline during the week due mainly to the share drop of blue chip companies... But investors expect the market to resume its upward trend soon," a bourse official said.
Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, one of the market's largest capitalisations, lost five dirhams in one week to close at 400 dirhams.
Wafabank, one of the liquid stocks, was traded at 537 dirhams, down from 546 dirhams a week earlier.
Speculation on the market predicted the bank would increase its capital but no decision has yet been announced, a broker said.
Morocco's largest private ONA Group lost two dirhams to close at 480 dirhams. ONA has a market capitalisation of 8.2 billion dirhams.
SNI, Morocco's second largest private conglomerate, remained stable for the second week at 560 dirhams.

SNI stagnation coincided with the announcement of 1995 consolidated results for the first time. It posted $43.7 million consolidated net profits in 1995 but gave no comparative figures for the previous year.
The week registered also the official announcement of the delisting of Omnium Marocain d'Investissement firm, traders said. The bourse has at present 46 listed companies including eight banks.
Traded volume on Friday on the official market was 15.9 million dirhams compared with 25.9 million dirhams last Friday.
